problem_statement: The Jekyll Documentation Theme project site is a real Jekyll build served as a multi-page static documentation site (a home page at /index.html, product landing pages such as /p1_landing_page.html, and topic pages such as /mydoc_introduction.html that all share the top navigation, sidebar, and footer). A recent design change added a genre-native 'Doc set browser' - an on-page finder that sits above the documentation topics and lets the reader filter the doc-set cards (Getting Started, Product 1, Product 2, Formatting) by category, with a live readout of the form 'Showing N of 6 . <Category>'. The finder is styled by css/docfinder.css, wired by js/docfinder.js, and its per-route presence is driven by the whitelist in _data/docfinder.yml. Three things regressed in the shipped state: (1) the finder's category-tab row is pinned to a fixed non-wrapping width and its topic grid uses fixed-width columns, so on a 390px phone the finder pushes the whole document far wider than the viewport and the home page overflows horizontally, while desktop and tablet still contain it; (2) the finder was meant to appear on the home page AND the introduction and Product 1 landing routes, but the shipped whitelist only renders it on the home page; (3) the category filter's readout no longer tracks the clicked tab. Repair the Doc set browser so the mobile home page has no horizontal overflow, the finder is present on all three intended routes, and the category readout stays in sync with the active tab - preserving the theme's blue documentation visual language, the six doc-set cards, and the desktop/tablet layout.
required_content: Repair the Doc set browser layout so the mobile (390px) home page has no horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth within 24px of the viewport), while keeping the desktop and tablet layouts intact.

Keep the five category tabs (All, Getting Started, Product 1, Product 2, Formatting) and the six doc-set cards (Getting started, Pages & permalinks, Product 1 overview, Product 1 sample, Product 2 overview, Alerts & callouts) present and legible after the repair.
Keep the Doc set browser present on all three intended routes: the home page (/index.html), the introduction topic (/mydoc_introduction.html), and the Product 1 landing page (/p1_landing_page.html).

Keep the category filter functional so the readout advances to the clicked set (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 . Product 1') and the grid shows only that set's cards, not frozen on 'Showing 6 of 6 . All doc sets'.
Preserve the Jekyll Documentation Theme content signals: the top navigation, the sidebar, the page body, and the footer wordmark, and keep the theme's blue documentation styling.
Keep the bundled local image images/company_logo.png as a browser-visible img element in the footer.
Do not remove content, add a framework/package-manager/backend/remote API/remote image/new dependency, or introduce console or network errors.
The repair must be a scoped responsive-layout + wiring fix, not a content rewrite, and must not change the doc-set card content or DOM structure across viewports.
design_constraints: Fix the finder's tab row and topic grid so the tabs wrap and the cards reflow fluidly on narrow viewports instead of pinning a fixed row width and fixed grid tracks; use stable responsive constraints and normal media queries.

Keep the Jekyll Documentation Theme visual language: the blue accent, clean bordered light cards, muted uppercase category labels, and a legible documentation hierarchy. Do not restyle the finder into an overlapping, collapsed, or illegible panel.
Render the Doc set browser on every intended route (home, introduction, Product 1 landing), not only the home page, so the cross-page documentation identity stays consistent.
Wire the category filter so the readout reflects the live set each time a tab is clicked; do not leave a stale readout that never updates while the grid stays unfiltered.
Do not use viewport-width font scaling, hidden-only text, placeholder images, remote media, or overflow-x:hidden hacks that leave the underlying fixed-width row overflowing the document.
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home, and mobile_home verify the documentation home page loads across breakpoints with no horizontal overflow after the repair.

mobile_home and mobile_finder verify the repaired Doc set browser fits a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow; the original-with-defect leg overflows about 1628px and a shallow non-fix still overflows about 288px.
desktop_finder verifies the doc-set browser keeps the blue documentation visual language with legible, non-overlapping cards and a readable active tab, not a collapsed illegible pile.
desktop_finder_p1 verifies the category filter's readout advances to 'Showing 2 of 6 . Product 1' and the grid filters after the Product 1 tab is clicked (interaction continuity).
desktop_intro and desktop_p1_landing verify the shared Doc set browser is present on the introduction and Product 1 landing routes, not only the home page (cross-page design continuity).
desktop_docs_page verifies an ordinary documentation topic page still renders the theme's navigation, body, and footer after the repair.

change_completion: The home page shows the Doc set browser with all five category tabs, six doc-set cards, and the live readout.
The category readout advances after a tab is clicked and the Doc set browser is present on the introduction and Product 1 landing routes as well as the home page.
design_consistency: The Doc set browser reads as a coherent Jekyll Documentation Theme design using the blue accent, clean bordered light cards, and muted category labels.
The finder is not restyled into an overlapping, collapsed, or illegible panel or an unrelated design language.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile home states have no horizontal overflow, clipped tabs, overlapped cards, or unstable grid widths.
Mobile keeps the Doc set browser readable in a wrapped tab row and single-column card rhythm with tappable controls.
regression: The top navigation, sidebar, page body, footer wordmark, and the theme's blue styling remain intact.
The bundled image images/company_logo.png remains browser-visible and no remote media or new dependencies are introduced.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a scoped design-continuity repair of the real Jekyll documentation site: it makes the Doc set browser's tab row wrap and its topic grid reflow so the 390px mobile home page has no horizontal overflow, keeps the finder on the blue documentation visual language with legible non-overlapping cards, keeps the finder present on all three intended routes (home, introduction, Product 1 landing), and keeps the category readout in sync with the active tab, while preserving the theme navigation, sidebar, footer, doc-set content, local logo, and desktop/tablet layout. Leaving the fixed-width non-wrapping row (baseline) or a shallow restyle that collapses the cards into an overlapping illegible pile, drops the finder from the introduction and Product 1 routes, and freezes the readout (bad) fails multiple gates: no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions (cross-page finder), and interaction_assertions (stale readout).
author_notes: Slot 271 was a ledger duplicate of slot_067 on MarketingPipeline/Simply-Docs and has been reassigned to the long-tail repo tomjohnson1492/documentation-theme-jekyll (the Jekyll Documentation Theme) for docs / Design Continuity / repair / cross_page, hardened to L4. The site is a real Jekyll build (jekyll build -> _site) served as a multi-page static documentation site. The native lever is the theme's own on-page 'Doc set browser' - a category filter over six documentation doc-set cards with a live count readout - placed above the topics where a docs site naturally hosts section navigation. Four orthogonal levers: (D6) a fixed-width non-wrapping tab row plus fixed-width grid columns cause mobile horizontal overflow; (D3) the bad leg collapses the card grid into an overlapping shingled pile with a near-white-on-near-white active tab so the whole finder region is illegible; (D2) the finder is dropped from the introduction and Product 1 routes; (D4) the category readout is frozen by a stale closure while the grid stays unfiltered. The reference repair fixes all four; the baseline fails D6/D3/D2 but passes D4; the bad leg fails all four. The doc-set card content and DOM are identical across all legs (the docfinder.html include and card data are shared); only the graded stylesheet css/docfinder.css, the wiring script js/docfinder.js, and the per-route whitelist _data/docfinder.yml differ. Remote CDN assets (bootstrap, font-awesome, jquery, anchor-js, commento, google-analytics) are vendored/neutralized as identical INFRA across all legs so the static pages stay console/network clean, and the theme's local logo image, svg-free bordered cards, and blue documentation palette are preserved.
